extracted.intended_audience: Rospatent/FIPS staff, patent librarians, patent examiners, and IP information managers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and operational criteria for maintaining, updating, providing access to, and using a national State Patent Collection (SPC) and associated Patent Examination Fund, plus related scientific and educational activities at a national patent institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of the State Patent Collection (SPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Patent Collection (SPC) is a set of information sources systematized and supplied with an information retrieval apparatus (IRA), relating to all industrial property objects on all types of carriers, as well as to registered computer programs, databases and integrated circuit topographies, including patent documents, patent-associated, patent-legal, regulatory and methodological, scientific and technical and reference literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPC must cover all industrial property objects and related literature across carriers (electronic, paper, micro) and include IRA support for retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative inventory and reporting of SPC size
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the total number of items in the SPC and annual increases (e.g., as of Dec 31, 2019 SPC contains 142.1 million copies; 2019 increase = 6.6 million).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide yearly statistics and comparisons to prior years; break down increases by source (e.g., foreign patent offices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Breakdown of SPC by information carrier
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and report SPC distribution by carrier type (electronic, paper, micro). Example figures: electronic 67.0% (95,222,125), paper 25.0% (35,439,248), micro 8.0% (11,416,571).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track carrier-specific holdings and update breakdowns regularly for management and planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breakdown of SPC by document type (national/foreign/non-patent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify and report SPC holdings by type: foreign patent documents, national patent documents, and non-patent documents (example: foreign 92.4%, national 7.4%, non-patent 0.2%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain separate tallies for national vs foreign materials; use for access and collection development decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: International exchange procedures for patent documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct international exchange primarily by uploading data from foreign Patent offices from FTP servers or other network resources; provide Rospatent's official publications to foreign offices via a special FTP server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operate automated data-upload mechanisms with partner offices, record volumes exchanged (e.g., 6.0 million docs uploaded in a year), and maintain exchange agreements with many offices/organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring completeness and intake recording
rubrics_metrics.description: FIPS Library department must constantly monitor SPC completeness, record incoming and uploaded foreign documentation, and track the quantitative state of the SPC overall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain logs and reports of incoming flows, detect gaps, and reconcile holdings against expected exchanges and subscriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of access via national electronic resources (NEB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide access to national patent documentation through the National Electronic Library (NEB); upload substantial historical patent collections (e.g., >2.5 million Soviet and Russian patent documents from 1924–2019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure online accessibility through FIPS website and mobile NEB platform; measure coverage relative to NEB total holdings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural division: Central Patent Fund (CPF) and Patent Examination Fund (PEF)
rubrics_metrics.description: SPC must be divided into two main parts: CPF (serves all categories of users) and PEF (designated to serve state intellectual property experts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define distinct collection development, access rules, and update policies for CPF and PEF according to user needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPF collection scope and historic holdings
rubrics_metrics.description: CPF includes collections of national (since 1814) and foreign patent documents of various depths, abstract and bibliographic publications on all industrial property objects, patent-legal collections, normative-methodical and reference books, and IRA to these collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain comprehensive historic and reference collections to serve a broad user base; include bibliographic and legal reference materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of searchable systems to users (PatSearch and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide users with access to the PatSearch search system and other modern patent information resources (Global Patent Index, EAPATIS, Questel Orbit, eLIBRARY) for conducting patent information research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure current subscriptions, user training, and remote/onsite access to multiple search platforms to support diverse research needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to external publishers and multidisciplinary databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide access to e-book patent and legal publications and other information resources (Edward Elgar, electronic library of dissertations, Web of Science, KluwerIPLaw, ScienceDirect, Scopus, SPRINGER NATURE, eLIBRARY).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate external publisher resources into the library's offerings and advertise availability to users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance of PEF by PCT Rule 34 and treaties
rubrics_metrics.description: The structure and composition of the PEF are governed by Rule 34 of the Regulations under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) and by bilateral interagency treaties and agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align PEF holdings and access rules with international obligations and agreements; document governance basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEF currency and platform updates
rubrics_metrics.description: To conduct patent examination, use modern automated patent information systems (PatSearch) regularly updated with national and foreign patent documents, and maintain access to databases such as STN Intrantinal, DWPI, SAEGIS, and Lexis Nexis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly refresh database holdings and ensure examiners have up-to-date access; renew subscriptions as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition away from updating paper PEF copies
rubrics_metrics.description: PEF on paper copies may be retained for holdings (e.g., 17.3 million copies) but is no longer being updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize electronic updates and plan preservation/access strategies for legacy paper collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of non-patent literature in PEF
rubrics_metrics.description: State examination requires non-patent information in the PEF such as scientific and technical, patent and legal or reference books and regular publications; provide interlibrary loan and electronic delivery upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure workflows to retrieve non-patent literature quickly (interlibrary loan, electronic delivery) to support examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of applications and contracts collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an integral collection of applications and contracts for results of intellectual activity and means of individualization; update holdings and determine storage periods (permanent/temporary), transferring items to state archives as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record volumes, distribute copies to departments as needed, review storage periods for items (e.g., examine 38,000 applications to determine storage period), and transfer to archives for permanent storage when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of providing patent information services
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide patent information services directly at Library service departments and remotely via information products on the FIPS website, processing written requests, and telephonic consultations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer both in-person and remote service channels; document service workflows and ensure responsiveness to written/phone inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: User access to multiple carriers and rare collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Library users must be provided access to information retrieval systems, patent and non-patent databases, patent documentation on paper and microcarrier, unique historical collections (e.g., Russian privileges 1814–1917), and patent-legal literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve and provide access to rare/historical items, supporting research and reference needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference and advisory services for patent searches and classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide references and advice on conducting patent searches, classification systems, using databases and other sources of patent information available in the Library and on the websites of Rospatent/FIPS and foreign offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff must be trained to advise on search strategies, classification use, and source selection; make guidance available onsite and online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical training on databases and electronic filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize practical classes on working with databases and training in electronic filing of applications, including test access to services for electronic filing of inventions, utility models, trademarks, computer programs, databases, and industrial designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run regular hands-on training sessions and provide test-access environments to build user competence in electronic submission systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic catalogue currency and link maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and update the electronic catalogue frequently (e.g., catalog updated every three days; as of Dec 31, 2019 it contained 352,086 records) and keep internet resource link lists current (e.g., 10,770 links; patent information browser links 5,760).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule periodic updates, maintain link integrity, and publish changes on the website quarterly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing user-request statistics and service indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish users' requests to information products and quantitative data on services (e.g., tables of orders and services) on the FIPS website and in annex tables to the Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track service requests, compile indicators (number of orders, main service types), and make aggregated data publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and dissemination of outreach materials and exhibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare patent information products, brochures, mobile and virtual exhibitions, and educational booklets for museum exhibitions and educational projects (examples provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SPC holdings to support public awareness campaigns, produce thematic abstracts and brochures, and post materials on NEB and FIPS sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective Information Dissemination (SDI) service for specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide SDI to specialists (e.g., automated distribution of information on new publications weekly to Directors and main specialists; service available in automated mode via ARM services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement automated SDI workflows, maintain subscriber lists, and deliver weekly digests (e.g., Digest on Intellectual Property and Related Areas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and Technological Council peer-review role and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A deliberative Council carries out peer review of issues and formulates suggestions on scientific, technical, legal and information activity; membership includes internal staff and external experts (example: 36 members including Doctors and PhDs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold regular meetings (e.g., 6 meetings with 30 reports), document decisions, and assign follow-up tasks based on peer review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research thematic areas under FIPS Thematic Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Research projects should address: legal protection and examination of IP objects; information technologies in the IP field; economic and organizational issues; development of educational activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align funded projects with institutional priorities and publish results that inform practice and legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outputs expected from research projects (methodologies and proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should produce actionable outputs such as proposals for changes in departmental methodology and regulatory acts, databases (e.g., legal service names), algorithms for automating examination tasks, approaches to paperwork for international registration, and analytical models for IP system evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver proposals, draft technical requirements (for software), indicator systems and calculation methodologies for practical implementation by Rospatent/FIPS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of professional training standards and competency frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop models for professional training in the IP field, including a list of specialists' competences, draft further education programs (compliant with national strategies), methodology for calculating staffing demand, and draft legal documents for specialist training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce curricula and competency lists, tie training to strategic workforce needs, and prepare legal/regulatory drafts to institutionalize training standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological recommendations and monitoring instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce methodological recommendations (e.g., on evaluation of intangible assets market value) and questionnaires for document quality evaluation for regional strategic development monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standardized instruments in regional/sectoral studies and supply them to requesting governmental bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical support for federal and regional bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide analytical materials, proposals, statistics, and reviews for federal executive bodies and regional administrations (e.g., analyses of patenting trends, suggestions for state programs, statistical data for forecasting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver tailored analytical notes, forecasts, and proposals upon request to inform policy and program development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational program structure and accreditation
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer education at multiple levels (university degrees, training for teaching/academic staff, further professional education) and maintain program accreditation (examples of student numbers and state accreditation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor student enrollment, graduation counts, and maintain compliance with national accreditation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: RSAIP research, publication and expert report expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Academy to conduct scientific research, collaborative projects, hold scientific events, prepare expert reports (e.g., 26 expert reports), and publish academic/practical journals (e.g., 'Copyright').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use applied research outputs in teaching and publish materials in recognized databases (e.g., Garant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Further professional education program offerings and participant targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement advanced training and professional retraining programs (example: 31 programs, 435 students; programs ranging 16–250+ academic hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design curricula of varying lengths, track student participation, and offer distance-learning options where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent attorney candidate training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide candidate training programs for patent attorneys across specializations (e.g., trademarks, inventions, computer programs, industrial designs) with specified cohort sizes (examples: 45, 47, 13, 8 graduates respectively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer specialized courses tailored to patent attorney certification streams and track completion statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal FIPS staff training and Expert-intern program
rubrics_metrics.description: Run continuous internal training per a Consolidated Plan (e.g., group sessions and departmental sessions) and operate 'Expert-intern' programs: training of experts for inventions/utility models (232 academic hours) and for trademarks (126 academic hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize training on new normative legal acts and fees; track participant numbers and assign trained interns to expert departments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary vocational training licensing compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Realize supplementary vocational programs under appropriate license (example: license series 77Л 01 No. 0008944 issued Dec 19, 2016) and start educational activity under license since 2017.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure vocational training programs operate under valid licensing and registration, and document license details for compliance.
